extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners, KIPO staff, applicants and patent attorneys practicing before the Korean Intellectual Property Office
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural rules and standards under the Korean Patent Act and subordinate statutes governing (A) service/notification of patent-related documents (methods, recipients, special rules, electronic service, service by publication, overseas service) and (B) payment, calculation, exemption and refund of official/patent fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documents subject to service related to examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents which affect the gain or loss of a patent right in a patent-related proceeding are defined as documents subject to service (examples include a certified copy of the decision to grant a patent, a notification of invalidation under Article 16(2), and a certified copy of the decision under Article 214(3) of the Patent Act).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such documents shall be notified/served by the prescribed procedures. Documents other than those subject to service shall be sent in the manner prescribed by the Commissioner of KIPO, but current practice treats many such documents the same as documents subject to service (including use of the Government Electronic Document System).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted methods of service
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods of service of documents include personal service, service by mail and service by publication (Article 18 of the Enforcement Decree).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 18(11) allows the Commissioner to prescribe sending methods for other documents; in practice dispatch boxes, administrative practice regulations and the PatentNet system are used similarly to service methods. Special service methods (see separate rubric) apply for certain rulings per the Postal Service Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal service procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Personal service is handing documents to the party or their representative in person; the examiner must obtain a receipt stating the date and name of the recipient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presentation of a receipt may be replaced by stamping the registered seal on the document service registry and registry of postage payment in the dispatch box and confirming them. Where recipient is not a patent attorney, the patent attorney’s registered seal and representative’s seal shall be stamped together (Regulation for Administrative Practices of Dispatch Box).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mail service procedure (registered mail)
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents shall be served by registered mail, except where a party or representative receives documents in person or via an information and communication network.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When served by mail, the receipt of the registered mail issued by the post office shall be placed in the file. Fees paid after the payment period shall be returned (see fees section). For overseas residents without an administrator, registered airmail is used and deemed served on mailing date (sending theory).

rubrics_metrics.name: Special service for written rulings/decisions on trial/retrial/revocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Written rulings or decisions on trial, retrial or revocation of a patent right must follow the special service method prescribed by the Postal Service Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, examiners may use information and communication networks to serve such rulings/decisions to persons who filed documents in electronic form. Article references: Postal Service Act, Enforcement Decree and Enforcement Rules of the Postal Service Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of recipient
rubrics_metrics.description: The recipient of served documents shall be the person to whom the documents are to be served: if an applicant has a representative, the representative is the recipient; if a sub-agent or representative was appointed mid-proceeding, service is to that sub-agent/representative unless special reasons exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where there are two or more representatives, the representative first written in the application receives documents, except for special reasons. If one representative has general power and another has special power, serve the one with special power first. Incompetents are served via legal representatives. If party is imprisoned, serve the head of the prison/detention house. If a representative designated to receive documents has been notified to the Commissioner, serve that representative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service location rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents shall be served to the domicile or place of business of the person to be served; where the person has reported another place, serve to that reported place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the place to be served changes, report without delay to the Commissioner. If a person refuses to receive documents without justifiable reason and service is thereby impossible, service is considered to have been made on the day of sending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service by publication — triggering conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Service by publication is used where documents cannot be served because the domicile or place of business of the person to be served is unclear (including where domicile cannot be confirmed even by using the resident registration number sharing system), or when the domiciles of all persons involved cannot be identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For juristic persons the resident registration number sharing system cannot be used; examiners must attempt to find the statutory domicile and serve at least once before resorting to publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service by publication — procedural steps before publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Before service by publication, the examiner must: (①) enter dispatch number and grounds for return into the data system and notify division heads; (②) confirm domicile using administrative data sharing; (③) if needed, try to confirm domicile by phone or other means; (④) send a guide for notification of change in applicant information with returned documents if a new domicile is identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If domicile still cannot be identified after these attempts, the examiner shall serve the returned documents by public announcement. If return was due to recipient's absence, the examiner may reattempt delivery to the original domicile before publication in some cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service by publication — timing and legal effect
rubrics_metrics.description: When documents are served by publication for the first time, the service becomes effective two weeks after disclosure in the patent gazette. Subsequent publications to the same party take effect on the following date of disclosure in the gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the address changes after publication and the proceeding is still active, documents must be resent; if the proceeding is terminated, respublishing is unnecessary. Statutory or designated periods start from the effective date by publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructions on post-publication delivery and re-service
rubrics_metrics.description: If after initial publication the examiner intends to deliver relevant documents to the same party and no notification of change was made despite a notice, and the grounds for return were ‘Recipient Absence’, ‘Moved’ or ‘Address Unknown’, the examiner shall immediately make service by publication rather than deliver by mail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a party requests direct delivery after service by publication, a receipt for a written application shall be stored in the file wrapper; for electronically-filed applications, examiners shall request the history of the written application and keep a receipt in each examination division.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple parties and publication (who to re-serve)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where there are more than two parties to be served and delivered documents are returned, the examiner shall serve the documents again to the other party rather than serve by publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If documents were delivered to a representative of more than two parties but were returned, an examiner shall not directly deliver documents to parties other than the representative because only the representative can conduct the proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service to overseas residents
rubrics_metrics.description: For overseas residents with a patent administrator, documents shall be served on the patent administrator. For overseas residents without an administrator, documents may be sent by registered airmail and are deemed served on the mailing date (sending theory).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This adopts the 'sending theory' for mail service to overseas residents; examiners must observe whether an administrator is present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of electronic documents
rubrics_metrics.description: If a person has notified use of electronic documents to KIPO, an examiner can serve documents through an information and communication network; service through the network has the same effect as service of written documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All documents may be served electronically except where special provisions in the Patent Act require otherwise (e.g., special service). Current practice uses the Government Electronic Document System for examination results that affect patent rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special service for certain adjudications/utility model matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjudication or decision on trial, review, ruling on establishment of non-exclusive license and revocation of patent or utility model rights shall be delivered by the special service method prescribed by the Postal Service Act; for electronically-filed persons the network may be utilized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to Article 15 of the Postal Service Act, Article 25 of its Enforcement Decree and Articles 62, 63 of its Enforcement Rules for the special service method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to pay official/patent fees (who pays)
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who performs a patent-related proceeding shall pay official fees. If the number of claims is increased by amending the specification after a person other than the applicant files a request for examination, the applicant shall pay the fees for examination of the increased claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment methods, deadlines and other necessary matters are prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry; Fee Collection Rules specify amounts and payment methods. Fees are fees for services provided by the State and differ from ordinary taxes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of official/patent fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Types/instances of fees related to examination include: application fee (patent, utility model, divisional, converted), priority claim fee, fee for request for examination (including reexamination, expedited), fee for change of applicant, fees for amendment, fee for extension of statutory/designated period, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The amount for each fee type is listed on the KIPO website; Fee Collection Rules Articles 2 and 3 define types and amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment timing, payer identification and accepted methods
rubrics_metrics.description: When documents are submitted, the document registration number is deemed the payer number; fees shall be paid to a bank collecting taxes or a post office by the following day of receipt of the documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees can be paid via electronic payment (Internet Giro) or in cash with Annexed Form No.1(2). When paid by mail, they must be by postal money order. Fees paid after the payment period shall be returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting claims for fee calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: In estimating fees for a request for examination, the number of claims shall be counted by each claim regardless of independent or dependent status; even if a claim depends on more than two claims, it is counted as one claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a request for examination is filed, claim count is based on the claims at the relevant time (initial, final after amendments, or at time of amendment submission). Examples are provided for scenarios where amendments occur before, at the same time, or after the request for examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional fees for claim-increasing amendments after examination request
rubrics_metrics.description: After making a request for examination, where fees for the request are increased because of amendment (e.g., new claims are added), the applicant must pay the additional fees when submitting the written amendment; fees for deleted claims are not refunded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calculation rules: (①) request at same time as filing — use initial claims if no amendment; ② where claims changed before request — use final claims after amendment; ③ where request and amendment submitted simultaneously — use claims after amendment; ④ where claims increased after request — count increased number regardless of deleted claims. Examples given (numeric).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of unpaid examination fees
rubrics_metrics.description: When fees for a request for examination are unpaid, an examiner shall order amendment; where deficiencies are not addressed after amendment, an examiner may invalidate the request for examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies to fees under the Fee Collection Rules (specific article references provided). Examiners have discretion to invalidate requests if payment requirements are not fulfilled after opportunities to correct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refunds of patent fees and official fees — qualifying cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent/official fees paid shall be refunded only upon payer’s request in specific cases, including: erroneous payments; portions for years after a patent revocation becomes final; portions after invalidation of patent term extension; official fees for filing/priority where application voluntarily withdrawn/abandoned within one month (with exceptions); certain request-for-examination refunds where withdrawal occurs before certain events; refunds for various trial-related withdrawals or dismissals (often half refunds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A detailed enumerated list (Article 84) specifies many refund-triggering events and related conditions (including which portions may be refunded). No refund claim may be filed after three years from notice to payer (see timeline rubric).

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline for refund claims
rubrics_metrics.description: No claim for refund of a patent fee or official fee may be filed after three years from the date when a person receives notice that the refund-triggering event applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If paragraph (1) of Article 84 applies, Commissioner or president of IP Trial and Appeal Board shall notify the payer; the 3-year limitation runs from that notification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption or reduction authority and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner of KIPO shall exempt or may reduce/exempt payment of certain patent/official fees (e.g., fees for State-owned applications, certain invalidation petitions; reductions for persons eligible under National Basic Living Security Act). A person seeking benefit must submit documents specified by Ordinance of the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each exemption/reduction's requirements must be met at the time of document submission; evidential documents and specific eligibility rules are enumerated (see complete/partial exemption rubrics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete exemption categories and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete exemption: certain persons (examples: medical care recipients under National Basic Livelihood Security Act; persons of national merit and surviving families; registered disabled persons; elementary/junior high students; persons aged 6–19; military service/public service workers) shall not pay application fees and request-for-examination fees for up to 10 cases per year and patent fees or utility model registration fees for the first three years when filing/registering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidential documents required (copies of ID booklets, certificates). Requirements must be satisfied at time of submission. Note: patent applications filed by certain state/public university special organizations are NOT exempt. Detailed table lists subjects, requirements and evidential documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial exemption for individuals, SMEs, and selected organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Partial exemption (reduction) of application fees, request-for-examination fees, patent fees for first three years, or utility model registration fees is available to individuals, SMEs, joint research between conglomerates and SMEs, public research organizations, technology transfer task forces, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For individuals, SMEs and certain organizations, 30% reduction applies to patent fee and utility model registration fees for years 4–9. Amounts less than 100 won are not included in exemption calculations. Applicants filing personally must be the inventor or designer to receive individual exemptions.
